title: add vpc control plane terraform multi-az interface endpoints peering route53
author: Priya Singh
description: Add a Terraform module and example configurations to provision VPC control plane networking for Private deployments across multiple AZs. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private in regulated environments require a repeatable, secure, multi-AZ topology that includes interface endpoints for control-plane services, cross-account VPC peering for hub-and-spoke setups, tightened security group policies, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation for service discovery. This PR implements: 1) a new modules/vpc-control-plane Terraform module (multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, route tables, security groups); 2) optional cross-account peering + route propagation and automated Route53 inbound/outbound delegated zone records; 3) examples for single-account and multi-account hub-and-spoke deployments with upgrade hooks for existing installations; 4) Helm chart minor values.yaml docs to toggle use of interface endpoints; 5) integration tests (local Terraform test harness + terratest stubs) and CI automation that runs lightweight plan/validate against a mocked AWS account. Checklist: - [x] module design doc + diagrams in docs/terraform/vpc-control-plane.md - [x] reusable variables and outputs for interface endpoints & peering - [x] idempotent plan for existing clusters (upgrade hooks) - [x] unit & integration test stubs - [x] docs + release notes - [x] terraform fmt & validate passing Notes: Route53 delegation requires IAM for route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets and cross-account role credentials; this PR includes an example AssumeRole config and guidance. The module defaults to interface endpoints for SSM, EC2, STS, and ECR (where applicable) and exposes a variable to disable services if customers prefer NAT/IGW paths. For security groups, the module creates a control-plane SG with limited ingress from known worker CIDR ranges and a managed egress policy for S3/ECR endpoints. This PR is conservative by default to avoid breaking existing private installs.
commits_summary: 3 commits: (1) terraform: add modules/vpc-control-plane with multi-az subnets, endpoints, SGs, peering and route53 helper; (2) examples: add single-account and multi-account hub-spoke examples and upgrade hooks; (3) docs/tests: add usage docs, terratest stubs, CI updates and changelog entry
ci_checks: integration: ran lightweight terratest stubs (plan-only) against mocked account
review_comments: Miguel: Requested tighter defaults for control-plane SG and explicit deny rules for wide egress during review. Aisha: Asked for clearer guidance on Route53 cross-account delegation and example AssumeRole policy; also requested terratest stubs be gated behind a CI flag to avoid AWS bill incursions. SRE Team: Verified the peering/route propagation approach matches our upgrade strategy and asked to add a migration hook to re-run route table associations post-upgrade. Author replies: tightened SG defaults, added explicit deny egress rules, added a secure AssumeRole example, gated terratest integration behind CI flag and documented upgrade hook behavior. Final: Approved by Miguel and Aisha after the follow-up commit.
release_notes: Add terraform module infra/terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane to provision multi-AZ control-plane networking for Private deployments. Includes interface endpoints, security group defaults, cross-account peering helpers, and Route53 private-hosted-zone delegation examples. See docs/terraform/vpc-control-plane.md for usage and upgrade guidance.
upgrade_instructions: For existing private deployments: 1) Review variables controlling endpoint creation (enable_interface_endpoints). 2) Follow docs/terraform/upgrade-hooks.md to apply peering and route propagation changes in a staged manner. 3) Run the provided migration script to reconcile route tables and Route53 delegation records after upgrade. The module exposes outputs to integrate with in-place upgrades.
notes: This PR intentionally defaults to conservative networking (no broad CIDR ingress) to minimize accidental exposure. The examples include minimal AssumeRole snippets for cross-account Route53 changes; customers must review and scope IAM before use. Follow-on work tracked in ENG-4956 will add automated smoke tests in a sandbox AWS account.
